subject: FY2022 Municipal Budget
overview: The Medford City Council met to address routine licensing, utility easements, administrative inquiries, collective bargaining agreements, and federal grant allocations. The Council approved the $191.9 million FY2022 municipal budget with amendments after extensive discussion with Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn.

items.title: Recognition of Outgoing TV Station Manager Patrick Gordon
items.summary: The Council commended outgoing TV station manager Patrick Gordon for his service during the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Common Victualler License for TownePlace Suites / Fairfield Inn & Suites
items.summary: Approved a petition for a common victualler license for Calwind Management doing business as TownePlace Suites / Fairfield Inn & Suites at 85 Station Landing.

items.title: Utility Grant of Location for Verizon on Greenland Extension
items.summary: Approved a grant of location petition from Verizon to provide utility access to the Greenland Extension.

items.title: Tufts University Easement at Cummings Center
items.summary: Approved an easement to Tufts University along College Avenue to construct accessible plaza connections and infrastructure for the new Cummings Center.

items.title: Police Superior Officers Union Collective Bargaining Agreement
items.summary: Approved an ordinance amendment establishing 2% annual wage increases for FY2020 through FY2022 under a newly negotiated agreement with the Medford Police Superior Officers Union, waiving the three readings.

items.title: Condolence Resolutions for Rick Sweeney and Paul Kavanaugh
items.summary: Approved resolutions expressing condolences to the families of retired firefighter Rick Sweeney and local volunteer Paul Kavanaugh.

items.title: Commendation for Retired Educator Teresa Castagnetti
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending Teresa Castagnetti upon her retirement after 45 years of service in the Medford Public Schools.

items.title: Commendation for Retired Educator Cheryl Maiorco
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending Cheryl Maiorco upon her retirement after 42 years in the Medford Public Schools special education department.

items.title: Legal Inquiry Regarding Municipal and School Building Naming Processes
items.summary: Approved a resolution asking the city solicitor for a ruling on whether the Council can establish a standardized naming ordinance for municipal and school facilities.

items.title: Congratulating Lynwood Engler on the MIT Collier Medal
items.summary: Approved a resolution congratulating Medford resident Lynwood Engler for receiving the MIT Collier Medal for his contributions to COVID-19 emergency response efforts.

items.title: CPA Appropriation for Royall House and Slave Quarters
items.summary: Approved an $80,000 Community Preservation Act appropriation to the Royall House Association for urgent roof, window, and chimney repairs.

items.title: Request for Information on Private Investigator Contract
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting full details, contract terms, procurement records, and funding sources regarding a private investigator hired by the administration.

items.title: Discussion on 2021 Municipal Preliminary Election
items.summary: Discussed a proposal to cancel the 2021 municipal preliminary election via a home rule petition to save funds and ensure voting consistency, ultimately placing the paper on file.

items.title: FY2021 Year-End Reserve Transfers
items.summary: Approved end-of-year interdepartmental transfers totaling $1,241,924.08 from surplus and free cash to cover account deficits, including snow and ice removal.

items.title: ARPA Grant Account Creation and Revenue Loss Appropriation
items.summary: Authorized the creation of an ARPA grant account and approved appropriations totaling $12.3 million to the General Fund and School Revolving Fund to replace Treasury-calculated COVID-19 revenue losses.

items.title: Approval of FY2022 Municipal Budget
items.summary: Approved the $191.9 million FY2022 municipal budget as amended, following debate over unclassified positions and a $55,000 reduction to contracted legal services.

items.title: Meeting Records and Knights of Columbus Recognition
items.summary: Approved meeting records from June 22 and June 23, 2021, and recognized the Knights of Columbus and Commander William Knight for local community service.
